tool: Codex CLI image tool via out/concepts/ui-011-r4/gen4.py (round 3's gen2.py call); cost 0 per image; no Runware or other paid service
concurrency: 2 workers, 5 generations, no timeouts or retries (44-60 s each)
method: Frames are composited, not generated whole: the Codex images are KIT SHEETS (icon hands, paper objects, orbs, signs) on flat magenta, keyed and cut; layouts, panels, rings, arcs, text and the pixel language are drawn in code (PIL, 3x supersampled; scripts in out/concepts/ui-011-r4/) over the real Handover plates. Reason: 28 layouts x 3 beats of exact numbers and positions cannot come out of one prompt per frame; round 3 made the same split.
plates: briefs/011/ui/plates/ (Latch): cafe-front-172430 (0:58 beat), office-door-1730 (the take), service-lane-1730 (the fight). Cell, guards, rivals, the response car and the camera cone are drawn by out/concepts/ui-011-r4/scene.py (the plates carry no cell capsules, no cones, no vehicles); they are identical under every variation.
palette_check: CIEDE2000 against cone red #e03a2f, guard amber #f0a020, rival violet #8a4fd0 (out/concepts/ui-011/de2000.py): every colour the HUD uses is >= 21.3 away (brass #99784d is the lowest, a thin line only; ink teal 34.3, cream 30.3, turquoise 42.4, seafoam 39.0). Sampled sprite colours (paper cream, orb glass) >= 23.6. FAILED and NOT USED: manila luggage-tag #e6cf9f (18.3 from guard amber) and peach tag #f1c4a6 (18.4); the paper language uses cream stock only.
footprint_metric: share of the 1920x1080 frame the HUD draws (alpha > 40) at the 0:58 beat: docked = the standing layout alone, total = everything incl. radial, price and icons. Cross-check by pixel difference against plate + world layer: round 3 d3-hybrid 12.0 %, d1 12.6 %, d2 6.3 %; round 4 v01 0.9 %, v06 1.3 %, v10 2.6 %, v23 5.9 % (difference method counts any changed pixel, so it reads a little higher than the alpha method).

generations.prompt: Game interface kit sheet for a real-time tactics game, one flat landscape 3:2 image. World: an optimistic atompunk city in an alternate history, a 1950s world that discovered atomic power centuries ago, so its culture and style are 1950s but its technology is centuries ahead; thinking machines and networks never came, so everything is clockwork, paper and enamel: stamped forms, punch cards, luggage tags, engraved dial plates; never a touchscreen, hologram, glass blur or sci-fi neon. Streamline Moderne and Googie, clean and prosperous. Canvas rule: the whole canvas is one flat, perfectly even, solid magenta #ff00ff with no scene, no shadow, no gradient and no vignette; magenta never appears inside a piece. No labels, no captions, no numbers, no text of any kind. Every piece is fully opaque, about the same size, in a regular grid with clear magenta gaps of at least 60 px between pieces and from the edge. STYLE: nine BLANK paper objects, no writing, no marks, no numbers on any of them. Flat, crisp and lightly paper-textured, each in one flat paper colour with a slightly darker edge line, like 1950s office and railway supplies; no shadows, no gradients. Colours: manila #e6cf9f, cream #f7f4ec, pale peach #f1c4a6, pale seafoam #bfe0d6; brass only as a thin eyelet or pin. Each about 220 px tall, in a grid of three columns and three rows, in exactly this order: 1 an upright manila luggage tag with a reinforced round eyelet at the top and a short loop of twine; 2 the same tag shape in pale peach with its twine; 3 the same tag shape in pale seafoam with its twine; 4 a wide rectangular cream shipping label with clipped corners and an eyelet at one end and twine; 5 a cream ticket stub with a perforated edge and a half-round notch; 6 a pale seafoam punch card with one clipped corner and a row of small round holes along the top edge; 7 a cream index card held at the top by a brass pin; 8 a narrow paper wrist-band strip in manila with a round snap at one end; 9 a small round cream gummed paper seal with a scalloped edge.
generations.used_for: k3 paper seals, tickets, index cards (paper language)

ROW 2: 6 watch (binoculars); 7 listen (an ear); 8 mislead (two footprints with a dashed arc bending away); 9 loop (a tape reel with a circling arrow); 10 reroute (a route line with a bend and an arrow). ROW 3: 11 enter (a door with an arrow going in); 12 take (a closed fist gripping, with an arrow carrying away); 13 fire (a pistol seen from the side); 14 next event (a double arrow, skip); 15 pause (two vertical bars). ROW 4, the four prices and the unknown: 16 cash (a coin seen at an angle); 17 time (a stopwatch); 18 Trail (a fingerprint); 19 Alert (a dome beacon lamp on a base with short rays); 20 unknown (a dotted ring holding a question mark).
